key_insight: Friction stir welding joint quality for AA6061-T6 is driven by interacting process parameters, with rotational speed, travel speed, and axial force jointly shaping strength and hardness.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical parameter window and shows that interaction-aware optimization can substantially improve weld mechanical performance and joint efficiency.
method: 3×3×3 full-factorial design on rotational speed, travel speed, and axial force
81 mechanical-test observations analyzed for UTS, yield strength, elongation, and hardness
Factorial ANOVA plus coded quadratic regression in IBM SPSS Statistics 31
evidence_signal: All three factors were significant for every response (p < .001), the Rotation×Travel interaction was significant throughout, and the best predicted UTS was 280.39 MPa at 1200 rpm, 80 mm/min, and 8 kN.
watch_item: The recommended settings are limited to the tested AA6061-T6, tool configuration, and experimental range, so they should not be generalized without validation.
paper_title: Optimization of Friction Stir Welding Parameters for Improving the Mechanical Properties of Aluminum Alloy Joints
